title: Chicken Goulash
description: A rich and comforting Continental chicken goulash made with tender marinated chicken, slow-cooked onions, paprika, bell peppers, and a creamy sour cream finish. Perfect served with spaetzle, mashed potatoes, or herbed rice.

ingredients.title: For the Chicken & Marinade
items: Boneless chicken thighs or breasts – 800 g (cut into 2-inch cubes)
Cayenne pepper – ½ tsp (adjust to taste)
Salt and cracked black pepper – to taste

ingredients.title: For the Goulash Base
items: Ripe tomatoes – 2 medium, peeled and chopped (or 200 ml tomato purée)
Chicken stock – 1 cup (or more as needed)
Dry white wine – 150 ml (optional but recommended)
Sour cream or crème fraîche – 100 ml

ingredients.title: For Finishing & Garnish
items: A drizzle of sour cream or a quenelle for plating
Buttered spaetzle, mashed potatoes, or herbed rice as accompaniment

instruction.title: Step 1 – Marinate the Chicken
steps: Combine olive oil, both paprikas, cayenne, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Toss chicken pieces well and marinate for at least 30 minutes (or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator).

instruction.title: Step 2 – Prepare the Goulash Base
steps: In a heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven, heat butter and olive oil over medium heat.
Add onions and sauté until golden brown (about 10–12 minutes).
Add garlic and caraway seeds, sauté for another 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the bell peppers and cook until soft, around 5–7 minutes.
Add tomato paste and cook until it deepens in color, then add chopped tomatoes.
Pour in white wine, deglaze the pan, and let it reduce by half.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Cook the Chicken
steps: Add marinated chicken pieces to the pan; sear lightly on all sides.
Add chicken stock and thyme, bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook gently on low heat for 40–45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and the sauce is rich.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Finish the Sauce
steps: Whisk sour cream with flour (if using), then temper it with a few tablespoons of the hot sauce before mixing it back into the goulash.
Simmer for another 5–7 minutes until creamy and well-blended.
Adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, or a hint more paprika.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Plating (Restaurant Style)
steps: Spoon a portion of the chicken goulash neatly onto the center of a warm plate.
Serve with a side of buttered spaetzle or smooth mashed potatoes.
Drizzle a swirl of sour cream and garnish with microgreens or parsley.
Optional: Add a few drops of paprika oil for a vibrant finish.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve with buttered spaetzle, mashed potatoes, or herbed rice.
Pair with a crisp Chardonnay or a light Pinot Noir.
Serve hot with a drizzle of sour cream.

chefTips: Depth of flavor: Use smoked paprika and slow caramelized onions—they are key to a deep, authentic goulash flavor.
For a luxurious touch: Add a small knob of butter and a dash of cream just before serving.
Wine pairing: Serve with a crisp Chardonnay or a light Pinot Noir.
